what: The estate's decision register (ADR 0044, T-7). Every action an agent takes is classified machine, model or judgment. The mode is DERIVED from the capability's own source wherever it can be (see bin/capability-index derive_intent_mode); this file holds only what cannot be derived: the judgement residue and the estate-level decisions. A `judgment` entry must name one of the four irreducibility kinds and say why no machine and no decision model can decide it. `bin/registry-gate` invariant I-6 refuses an entry that lies.

irreducibility_kinds.value-tradeoff: two goods the estate cannot rank without a human (founder wellbeing vs blast radius vs cost)
irreducibility_kinds.irreversible: the action cannot be undone, or is outward-facing
irreducibility_kinds.novel: no precedent in the estate and no rule that covers it
irreducibility_kinds.low-confidence-escalation: a decision model returned below its calibrated confidence floor

decisions.decision: Which failure in the estate gets the next unit of work?
decisions.justification: The order is a trade-off between the founder's wellbeing, the blast radius of the failure and what the estate can carry in parallel. The evidence can rank candidates on each axis separately; it cannot say which axis wins this week, and getting it wrong spends the founder's attention on the wrong fire.

decisions.decision: What the estate should become next: the target architecture and the sequence of waves.
decisions.justification: The epic's Phase C is a vision lock and its exit criteria are the founder's own sequence (AGENTS.md, epic section 25). No measurement of the estate can say which of two coherent futures it should walk toward; that is a value choice with a technical component, not a technical choice.

decisions.decision: Whether an irreversible or outward-facing action happens at all.
decisions.justification: The action cannot be undone and it reaches outside the estate (a public post, a spend past the agreed line, a deletion of state someone else owns). A machine can prove the action is well-formed and within policy; it cannot decide that the estate should be the one to do it.

decisions.decision: What to do when a decision model returns below its calibrated confidence floor.
decisions.justification: The floor (JEV's default_confidence_floor, 0.7) decides what the machine may answer. It cannot decide the escalated case: the research is explicit that a judge's confidence is not its correctness (arXiv 2508.06225, 2606.03043), so the escalated answer is a person's, and the person is named by the model's confidence band.

decisions.decision: Whether a change is inside the claim, which lane a task belongs in, how risky a diff is.
decisions.justification: The estate's one decision layer (ADR 0030) returns a typed value with a calibrated confidence, and a machine can check that the value is well-formed and inside the floor. What it cannot do is be right; the confidence is the model's own, so the mode is a model and not a machine.

decisions.decision: Which hypotheses are worth racing, and with what priors.
decisions.justification: Proposing a hypothesis is a reading of evidence and a bet on its likelihood: a model writes it. The race that follows is deterministic (the probes are commands, the posterior is arithmetic), so the proposal is the model part and the disposal is the machine part, and they are two decisions, not one.

decisions.decision: Whether a repository is created in public, in the estate's name.
decisions.justification: A public repository is outward-facing and cannot be un-published; the estate's own description of this intent says a human reviews and merges. A machine can prove the command is well-formed, and that is all it can do: whether the estate should be the one to publish is the founder's.

decisions.decision: What to do about a situation the estate has no precedent for and no rule that covers.
decisions.justification: By definition there is no rule to apply and no model trained on this estate's answer, so no machine decision is available. The residue is real only when it is written down: this entry exists so that 'we had no precedent' is a recorded reason rather than an unexamined habit.

decisions.decision: Whether a reconciliation the spine woke actually succeeded.
decisions.justification: The spine (EFDA) wakes a workflow from a Flux event, and the workflow's first act is to read the reconciliation status the event is about. That is a state fetch with a deterministic answer, and the estate already holds the capability that makes it (flux-status). The workflow that runs it is the trigger, not the decider.

decisions.decision: Which branch carries a change, and when it is merged.
Whether a change's CI is green, and which job failed if it is not.
What the remote actually says: pull requests, check runs, comments, files.
How risky a diff is, and whether it needs the full suite.
Which hypothesis explains a failure, raced rather than argued.
decisions.justification: The probes are commands and the posterior is arithmetic over their evidence, so the race disposes deterministically: the same probes and the same priors give the same ranking. The model proposes the hypotheses (dec:propose-hypotheses) and the machine disposes of them, and an errored probe is UNKNOWN rather than support, which is the part that makes the answer honest.

decisions.decision: What is wrong with a diff, proposed by a model and disposed of by deterministic checks.
